facts.quote: As predicted by the Napoleon complex, we conclude that (relatively) shorter men show greater behavioral flexibility in securing resources when presented with cues that they are physically less competitive.
facts.text: Psychologists remain divided over the validity of the Napoleon complex, with evolutionary researchers arguing short men display indirect resource competition while other behavioral studies demonstrate tall men are more physically aggressive.

facts.quote: In 1815 an English captain described him as 'a remarkably strong, well-built man, about five feet seven inches high'.
facts.text: British Royal Navy Captain Frederick Lewis Maitland documented in 1815 that Napoleon was a well-built man standing roughly five feet seven inches tall upon surrendering aboard HMS Bellerophon.
